chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi narrated to me from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his ancestors, peace be upon them, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Offering condolences inherits Paradise."

key_terms.التَّعْزِيَةَ: Condolence; the act of comforting the bereaved
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise; the eternal abode of bliss
key_terms.تُورِثُ: Inherits; causes one to inherit as a reward

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for offering condolences in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the act of *ta'ziyah* (condolence) is not merely a social courtesy but a direct path to Paradise, reflecting the high status of comforting the bereaved in Shia tradition. It underscores the spiritual merit of alleviating grief, linking interpersonal compassion with eternal reward.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors that the   Holy   Prophet   (s.a.w.s.)   said,   “Saying   words   of condolence is a way to enter Paradise.”
